title: Context / Scope of the Organisation
content:
SECTION 1 - CONTEXT / SCOPE OF THE ORGANIZATION

1.0 CONTEXT / SCOPE (4.1 / 4.2 / 4.3 / 4.4)

This Manual is intended to demonstrate to the customers of Ultimate Laser Pty. Ltd., that the organization has the capability to control its activities through the application of effective Systems which conform to the requirements of:

ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems

ISO 14001 Environmental Management Systems

ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety Management Systems

The Company provides the planning and control structures required to produce conformance to Quality, Environmental and OH&S requirements and a commitment to provide a safe and healthy work environment, continual improvement and prevention of pollution.

The Company also takes into account the needs of various interested parties

i.e. Directors, Employees, Suppliers, Customers, Communities, Work Safe, General Public, Regulators and Governments and which of these needs become its compliance obligations.

The Company has identified the risks to business continuity as; competitors, loss of revenue, major equipment failure, major power outages and loss of key personnel.

The Quality / Environmental / OH&S Systems described in this Manual applies to the manufacture and supply of laser, water jet and oxy cut components with the additional capability of arranging supply of finished goods and components with outsourced processes of forming, machining and plating.

The following pages describe the Quality / Environmental / OH&S Management Systems, organization and structure, responsibilities and authorities of the Management and staff of Ultimate Laser Pty. Ltd.

As Ultimate Laser does not design product (ISO 9001:2015 Section 8.3 Design and development of products and services) is not applicable.

1.1 AUTHORIZATION

This Systems Management Manual has been approved for issue and use by

Mr. Peter Craciunoiu

Managing Director of Ultimate Laser Pty. Ltd.

Date: October 5th 2018

title: Planning
content:
SECTION 2 - PLANNING

2.1 PLANNING IDENTIFICATION AND CONTROL OF RISKS AND OPPORTUNITIES, HAZARDS, ENVIRONMENTAL ASPECTS (6.1 / 4.3.1)

Top Management of Ultimate Laser Pty. Ltd. take responsibility for determining the risks and opportunities that need to be addressed enabling the organization to achieve its intended result(s) regarding the control of quality performance, environmental performance and OHS activities and services of which we would be expected to have an influence on.

2.1.1 COMPLIANCE OBLIGATIONS (6.1.2 / 6.1.3 / 9.1.2)

Top Management take responsibility for setting up safe systems of work to eliminate or minimize the risk of Health, Safety and Welfare to employees, contractors, visitors and general public

Top Management also take the responsibility of complying with all applicable laws, regulations and standards and apply standards that minimize any adverse quality or environmental impacts resulting from its operations, products and services

Top Management also take into account the environmental aspects of its activities, products and services that it can control and those that it can influence and their associated environmental impacts.

2.1.2 OBJECTIVES AND TARGETS (6.2 / 4.3.3)

Top Management shall ensure that Quality / OH&S / Environmental Objectives where relevant are established and reviewed

When establishing and reviewing its objectives, Top Management shall consider its compliance and other requirements, opportunities, hazards and risks, aspects and impacts, technological options, operational and business requirements.

Management plans for achieving its objectives and Targets shall include:

Designation of responsibility for achievement of objectives and targets at relevant functions and levels

Outlining the means and time frame by which objectives and targets are to be achieved

2.1.3 RESOURCES (7.1 / 7.1.2)

Top Management shall identify and provide the resources required to implement, communicate, maintain and continually improve their Quality / OH&S and Environmental Management Systems.

Resources include human resources and specialized skills, organization infrastructure technology and financial resources

title: Quality Policy
content:
SECTION 3 - QUALITY POLICY

ISO 9001:2015 REFERENCE 5.2

QUALITY POLICY

Ultimate Laser is committed to achieving high Quality standards in developing, manufacturing and selling specialist products and services to our chosen markets.

We will actively set out to: -

Manufacture all of our products (or to provide services) Right First Time to deliver them On Time in Full and to achieve complete Customer Satisfaction.

Understand our customers current and future Quality Objectives for the products and services we supply. Our logo is a symbol of Quality.

Provide the resources to develop our Management Systems, the skills of all Ultimate Laser employees and our technical and equipment capabilities so that we meet or exceed these Customer Quality Objectives based on the principal of “Right First Time”.

Involve all of our people in the Quality Process, since they control our performance. We will do this by leadership, communication and motivation, training and empowerment in Quality matters.

Involve our suppliers of goods and services in the process by working with them to establish, achieve and monitor agreed Quality Objectives.

Practice and promote the conservation of resources to minimize wastes, improve processes and protect the environment.

Comply with all legal and regulatory requirements

Ensure this Policy is available and is communicated, understood and applied within the organization

This Policy will be underpinned by a commitment both to our established ISO 9001:2015 Quality Assurance Systems and a continuous improvement in Operational and Management Procedures in the light of best practice and will be available to relevant interested parties as appropriate.

Peter Craciunoiu

MANAGING DIRECTOR

Date: October 5th 2018

title: Environmental Policy
content:
SECTION 4 - ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY

ISO 14001:2015 REFERENCE 5.2

ENVIRONMENTAL POLICY

Ultimate Laser P/L has achieved a high standard of environmental care in conducting its business its approach to environmental management seeks continuous improvement in performance by taking account of evolving scientific knowledge and community expectations.

Specifically, it is Ultimate Laser’s policy to:

Conduct operations in a manner that preserves the environment and protects our employees, neighbours and customers from injury and illness.

Comply with all applicable laws, regulations and standards, uphold the spirit of the law and where laws do not adequately protect the environment, apply standards that minimize any adverse environmental impacts resulting from its operations, products and services.

Communicate openly with government, our clients and the community on environmental issues and contribute to the development of policies, legislation and regulations that may affect Ultimate Laser.

Ensure that its employees and suppliers of goods and services are informed about this policy and are aware of their environmental responsibilities in relation to Ultimate Laser business.

Ensure that it has management systems to identify, control and monitor environmental risks arising from its operations.

Practice and promote the conservation of resources to minimize wastes, prevention of pollution, improve processes and protect the environment from pollution.

Ensure that this Policy is maintained as documented information and is communicated and understood within the organization.

Ensure that this Policy is available to all interested parties.

Peter Craciunoiu

Managing Director

Date: October 5th 2018

title: OHS Policy
content:
SECTION 5 - OHS POLICY

ISO 45001:2018 REFERENCE 5.2

OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH & SAFETY POLICY

Obligations

Ultimate Laser recognizes its moral and legal responsibility to provide a safe and healthy work environment for employees, contractors, customers and visitors ((Victorian Occupational Health and Safety Act). This commitment extends to ensuring that the organizations operations do not place the community at risk of injury, illness or property damage.

Objectives

Ultimate Laser will:

Achieve the highest safety standard

Provide and maintain a safe workplace, plant and system of work

Provide written procedures, instructions and maintain records to ensure safe systems of work

Ensure compliance with legislative requirements and current industry best practice

Provide information, instruction, training and supervision to employees, contractors and customers

to ensure their safety

Provide support, consultation and assistance to employees

Eliminate Hazards in the workplace

Responsibilities and Accountabilities

Each Management representative is responsible and accountable for implementing and reviewing this policy in their area of control

Management is responsible for:

The provision and maintenance of the workplace in a safe condition

Involvement in the development, promotion and implementation of Health and Safety Policies and Procedures

Training employees in the safe performance of their assigned tasks

The provision of resources to meet Health and Safety commitment

Promoting a safety culture

Ensuring that this Policy is communicated and understood by all employees

Employees are to:

Take care of themselves and others, follow all Health and Safety Policies and Procedures

Report all known or observed hazards to their immediate Supervisor or Manager

Application of the Policy

This Policy is applicable to Ultimate Laser in all its operations and functions

Consultation

Ultimate Laser is committed to continuous improvement, consultation, communication and co-operation between Management and Employees. Management will consult with elected employee Health and   Safety Representatives and Employees in any workplace change that will affect the Health and Safety of any of its employees.

This Policy shall be communicated and understood and applied within the organization and shall be available to relevant interested parties as appropriate.

Peter Craciunoiu

Managing Director   Date: 5-10-18

title: Responsibility and Authority
content:
SECTION 7 - RESPONSIBILITY AND AUTHORITY

The principal responsibilities and authorities for Quality, Environmental and OH&S control of the organization are contained in this section. Any changes to the delegation of responsibilities and authorities shall be by means of a specific instruction in writing.

7.1 MANAGING DIRECTOR

The Managing Director has overall responsibility and authority for the management of the organization and shall be responsible for the organizations administration. He shall direct the activities of employees in the area of prevention of pollution, compliance with applicable legal requirements and to continual improvement.

The Managing Director shall be responsible for ensuring that the need to meet Quality, Environmental and OH&S requirements and objectives are consistent with the Quality, Environmental and OH&S Policies.

Communication with any interested parties regarding Ultimate Lasers significant Quality / Environmental / OHS responsibilities shall be the Managing Directors sole responsibility and if appropriate, any decisions made shall be documented and maintained as records.

7.2 OPERATIONS MANAGER

The Operations Manager has the authority and is responsible for the day-to-day operations of the organization. He shall be responsible for the designation of responsibility for achieving objectives and targets at relevant functions and levels of the organization and the means and time frame by which they are to be achieved.

This includes the establishment and maintenance of Quality, Environmental, OH&S policies, objectives and responsibilities within the organization and along with Top Management shall be responsible for the review of the Quality, OH&S, Environmental Systems and is authorized to control all technical aspects of the organizations operation, including ensuring that legal and technical requirements are met as required.

7.3 QUALITY MANAGER

The Quality Manager has the authority and is responsible for the effective operation of the Quality, OH&S, Environmental Management Systems and reports directly to the Managing Director on all Quality, OH&S, Environmental matters. He is authorized to implement and monitor the organizations Systems, Targets and Objectives and shall establish and periodically review the organizations Internal Audit schedule, arrange audits, set new Objectives, Targets and recommend corrective, action to effect improvements and verify the effectiveness of such activities. He shall also be responsible for communicating along with other relevant personnel with external auditors (certification, customer).

7.4 PRODUCTION SUPERVISOR

The Sales Manager has the authority and is responsible for the day-to-day sales management of the organization.

The Sales Manager along with Top Management shall be responsible for the review of all technical aspects of the organization’s operations including ensuring that customer specifications and technical requirements are met.

The Sales Manager has the authority for the preparation of quotations and shall prepare estimates of all costs associated with each inquiry in consultation with other personnel as required.

The Sales Manager shall also be responsible for approving purchases on behalf of the organization to maintain the supply of raw materials, components and services.

7.5 SALES MANAGER

The Production Supervisor is responsible to the Operations Manager for planning and supervising the production operations of the organization, ensuring expenditure is minimized for continued growth and profitability.

He shall be specifically responsible for:

Managing the operations within the factory

Liaison with Purchasing, regarding to ensure consistency in manufacturing and deal with “Urgent” and “Special Requests”

Overview regular maintenance schedule and acquisition of spare parts

Planning and allocation of all jobs through the manufacturing processes including final inspection and packing

Ensuring stocks of all raw materials are continuously reviewed and are sufficient to meet production requirements

Authorize the stopping of production in the event of a non-conformance

Ensure all organization procedures are followed

Apply the principals of OH&S in the workplace, monitor compliance of regulations

Understand and apply the relevant Quality Procedures and Work Instructions

Work with others in a team

7.6 DIRECT LABOR

Each and every works operator is responsible to the Operations Manager for the safe and satisfactory performance of his assigned duties in accordance with the organizations Quality / OH&S / Environmental Policies and Procedures. All

employees are required to report any incidence to their appropriate Supervisor.

title: Internal and External Communication
content:
SECTION 8 - INTERNAL COMMUNICATION

The organization shall ensure communication between its various levels and functions regarding the process of the Quality, Environmental and OH&S Management Systems and their effectiveness (notice boards, emails).

Regular communication meetings shall be held with all personnel.

8.1 EXTERNAL COMMUNICATION

For communication with any interested parties regarding Ultimate Lasers significant Quality / Environmental / OHS responsibilities shall be the Managing Directors sole responsibility and if appropriate, any decisions made shall be documented and maintained as records.

Internal communications are achieved via regular meetings, memoranda and notice boards. Effectiveness of internal communication regarding all issues affecting the business shall be reviewed during Management Review.

3.5 External Communication

3.6 	Continual Improvement

The Management team reviews the suitability, adequacy and effectiveness of the Quality / Environmental / OH&S Management Systems. The expected outcome of the Management Review is:

Assessing continual improvement of the systems and processes at planned intervals.

Decisions and actions related to possible changes to Quality / Environmental / OH&S Policies, Objectives, Targets and any other elements of the Quality / Environmental / OH&S systems consistent with the commitment to continual improvement.

Resource needs.

3.7      Management Review Agenda

Typical agenda items to be addressed at this review meeting are, but not limited to:

(Note: In the context below, the purpose of review is to analyse the suitability, effectiveness and whether an improvement can be made of the stated subject at each point).

Review actions from previous Management Review.

Review the Nonconformance Reports (NCR’s) raised since last meeting and status of outstanding NCR’s.

Review communication(s) from external and interested parties including complaints and effectiveness of the Quality / Environmental / OH&S Management Systems in general, including any changes affecting the Quality, OH&S or Environmental Policies.

Review organization goals / objectives and corrective action issues i.e. review Business Plans / Aspects and Impacts

Review internal and external audit results including characteristic/trends of

processes and any resulting opportunities for corrective action.

Review the Quality, Environmental and OH&S performance of the organization.

Review training needs and resource issues

Are organization structure, authorities and responsibilities current and stable?

Review the effectiveness of internal communications between various levels of   the organization.

Review the extent to which objectives and targets have been met.

3.7    Management Review Agenda cont.

Review changing circumstances, including developments in legal and other requirements related to its Quality, Environmental and OH&S requirements.

Review recommendations for improvement.

Review Risks and Opportunities.

Review Competitors.

title: Safety Management Hazard Procedure
content:
2.11

SAFETY MANAGEMENT HAZARD PROCEDURE

The 4 Step Approach to Safety Hazard Management

Step 1 Identify the Hazards

Step 2 Assess the Risks

Step 3 Control the Risks

Step 4 Continuously Review

The following information provides general guidelines which can be used to identify safety hazards and effectively manage them.

Step 1: Identify the Hazards

Anything that has the potential to harm the health or safety of people at work, visitors to the workplace and the public.

The Safe Work Instruction on the machines or processes, provide a simple identification of   hazards within our workplace (compiled using JSA’s / Plant Hazard Checklists).

Using JSA’s (Job Safety Analysis), Plant Hazard Checklists the OH&S Committee and other personnel will look at each of our work activities and begin to prioritise the risks associated with each area.

When assessing what these risks might be, see how these might apply to our workplace and activities. An example might be manual handling of products. Possible hazards may be equipment, manual handling, mobile plant, floors.

Step 2: Assess the level of Risk

All work activities have some potential for causing injury or illness. What we need to do is look at all the areas of our work and identify which of these activities have a high potential or likelihood of causing injury or illness.

Many of the potential hazards are likely to be low risk. We will need to prioritise and focus on high-risk issues initially. Examples of common high-risk areas are where there is constant lifting powered machinery in operation, guarding, mobile plant operation forklifts and cranes.

Lack of maintenance is also something that needs to be considered. Poor plant, machinery or equipment maintenance can result in hoses splitting, oil spills and metal parts shearing.

In extreme cases, some equipment can explode or catch fire.

When you use the JSA’s / Plant Hazard Checklists you have the opportunity to assess the level of risk, e.g. high / medium / low and spell out what measures you will take to control these risks

It is always better to first consider eliminating the hazard rather than adopt a band-aid solution. For example, providing P.P.E. may not be of much use if a machine explodes.

Step 3: Control the Risks

Any assessment of the workplace safety hazards may result in several high-risk areas. These should be regarded as Top Priority and will need to have some planned action or procedure to eliminate or control them. You will need to determine how we control them.

There are some very obvious measures that can be taken such as:

Ensuring all plant is fitted with relevant safety gear/guarding

Only trained staff operate machinery, cranes and hoists

Licensed operators only operate forklifts

All personnel have suitable PPE

Hierarchy of Controls

Hazards should be dealt with in the following order:

a) Eliminate – Workplace

b) Substitute – Workplace

c) Isolate - Workplace

d) Engineer out - Workplace

e) Safe work practice - Workplace

f) PPE – Person

Whatever the high-risk areas are, we must develop procedures to eliminate or control them. The Plant Hazard Checklists / JSA’s will help identify, assess and list for action any high-risk safety hazards.

Once you have identified the hazards and agreed on the action to be taken you should record these on the Plant Hazard Checklists / JSA’s.

Step 4: Continuously Review

We will need to review how well our hazards are controlled.

You will also need to look for new hazards as they are constantly changing with new personnel, procedures and machinery being introduced into the workplace. Ultimate Laser shall put in place a continuous review process involving all personnel to ensure that all hazards are identified and addressed as they are known.

A small workplace safety committee shall be established and is a very effective way of reviewing the process and identifying any new hazards.

Safety hazards should be monitored and continuously reviewed and a formal process of reporting new hazards will be encouraged from all personnel. Similarly regular staff communication meetings will be programmed at which OH&S issues are a standing agenda item.

Once again, all personnel will be encouraged to contribute to the discussion on safety hazards, whether old or new and management will use these meetings to report on hazards checked or fixed.

POTENTIAL HAZARDS

Potential Workplace Hazards

The following pages provide an overview of potential hazards in the metal working industry.

There are 14 hazard headings with some practical descriptions of things to look out for or consider. This is not a comprehensive list, but gives some clear indicators to aid in identifying hazards.

Safe Working Instruction

The Safe Working Instruction sheet identifies some of these hazards in key operational areas. As a first step, this sheet is a very useful tool for helping all personnel identify hazards in each operational area in the workplace.

For instance, in metal working, manual handling is an important area to look at as proper lifting procedure must be employed when handling material.

There may be some operations that are not covered by this list. If this is the case amend the list accordingly.

Plant Hazard Checklists / JSA’s

Following your identification of hazards, an assessment of the risk and any necessary actions will need to be undertaken, the Plant Hazard Checklists / JSA’s allow personnel to determine the level of risk for each hazard and agree on action to be taken

These forms are used to manage and review safety and health hazards and are a formal record of the company’s performance.

POTENTIAL WORKPLACE HAZARD BY TYPE

A Hazard is something that has the potential to harm the health, welfare and safety of people at work or visitors to the site.

Not all health and safety risks are obvious.

The metal working industry has obvious risks (i.e. back injury, electrocution and chemical exposure).

Potential Hazards:

1) Manual Handling and lifting

Repairing and lifting of tools and dies

Handling of awkward goods

Positioning and lifting of material in machines

Handling of materials during processing

Lifting or moving products, stock bins, tubs and stillages

Loading for transport, lifting and stacking boxes and loading trucks

Not wearing PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) such as gloves

Not using the appropriate lifting equipment

Inadequate training, skill or capability of people undertaking physical work

Repetitive lifting tasks, especially twisting while lifting, heavy lifting and lifting away from the body centreline

2) Working with Machinery

Unsuitable or inadequate guarding

Lifting or moving products

Repetitive movements, especially twisting and reaching tasks

Electrical apparatus in wet areas

Not wearing the appropriate Personal Protective Equipment

Improper use of machinery

Tripping over material, cables and equipment

Slipping on water, oil or coolant spillages

Unsecured gas bottles

Inadequate training, skill or capability of people operating machinery

3) Working in proximity to operations

Poor housekeeping, tripping or slipping hazards

Over turning of stacked materials, cramped environments

Moving and lifting of goods and products

Working around or near machinery

Working alone in a risky environment

Not wearing Personal Protective Equipment

Incorrect loading / unloading of materials and goods to and from pallets and stillages

Having flammable / toxic materials near welding / grinding

4) Welding

Electric shock

Not following standard operation procedures

Exposure to welding arc (i.e. radiation burns)

Tripping hazards (i.e. leads, cables, materials and equipment0

Exposure to welding flashes and spatter burns

Not using appropriate welding screens

Unsecured gas bottles

Not wearing Personal Protective Equipment

5) Using power and hand operated tools

Tool design and the misuse of tools

Safe storage of tools

Condition of hand and power tools (i.e. chuck, leads, blades etc.)

Operators not trained in the correct use of power tools

Safety attachments removed or altered

Inadequate or no signage

Not wearing Personal Protective Equipment

6) Using vehicles, forklifts and mobile platforms

Operator training and competency

Surface condition (i.e. pot-holed, slippery, steep gradients etc.)

Persons not seated correctly

Not wearing seat belts

Getting on or off vehicles and mobile platforms

Vehicles left unattended with engines running and / or handbrakes not engaged

Poor maintenance of vehicles and equipment

Pedestrian traffic around vehicles

Excessive speed of vehicles

Exceeding rated load capacity of forklifts or platforms

not wearing Personal Protective Equipment

7) Using chemicals

Not reading and understanding how each chemical is used

Poor labelling of chemical substances

Poor handling and storage practices

Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS’s) not being read and understood by operators

Not wearing Personal Protective Equipment

8) Handling of Stock (raw material, work in progress and finished goods)

Not reading and understanding how each chemical is used

Cuts and punctures from sharp edges and burrs

Strapping machine hazards (i.e. cuts, pinch points, etc.)

Using box cutters, tin snips or other tool to open packages

9) Working with electricity

Electricity around water or moist environments

Poorly designed facilities, with unsupported cables

Damaged extension leads, cables, junction boxes and overloaded circuits

Improper placement of equipment and fittings

10) Office Areas

Lighting

Ventilation

Seating and work surfaces

Noise and disruptions

11) Employees

No Induction prior to site entry

Not understanding the hazards associated with the worksite

Inadequate or no safety signage

Unfit for work due to injury / illness

Dangerous behaviour or practice

Under the influence of drugs or alcohol

12) Visitors (clients, suppliers, contractors and friends)

No Induction talk prior to site entry

Not wearing Personal Protective Equipment such as safety glasses and ear plugs

Unsupervised visitors

No understanding of the hazards associated with the worksite

Inadequate or no safety signage

13) Facilities

Conditions of floors, walls, doors and roofs

Safety signs

Emergency Exits, evacuation and assembly points

Access and egress

Lighting

Ventilation

Storage and access

Waste removal

14) Emergencies

Explosions

Access to all areas

Injured persons

Inadequate or poorly maintained emergency equipment

Fire control, evacuation and assembly

title: Aspect / Impact Procedure
content:
ASPECT / IMPACT PROCEDURE

PURPOSE:

The purpose of this procedure is to define the mechanism for identifying and assessing environmental aspects over which

Ultimate Laser has control and influence. It is a formal link between any identified legal requirements and aspects and impacts.

1	SCOPE:

The scope of this procedure contains requirements of

ISO 14001:2015 clause 4.1 / 4.2 / 4.3

2	DEFINITIONS:

2.1 Aspect

Material, equipment or activity with the potential to cause environmental harm.

2.2 Impacts

Situation which may give rise to actual harm (e.g. release of oils,

chemicals into storm water system because of location of the facility).

2.3 Environmental at Risk (Effect)

Environmental media which may be affected under a specific risk

scenario:

SW: Surface Water i.e. Discharge to rivers and other controlled waters

State Environmental Protection Policy – Ground Waters of Victoria

S160

TE: Trade effluent i.e. Possible damage to sewers and sewage treatment

works.

A: Air Emissions i.e. Possible toxic or odour releases

State Environmental Policy – Ambient Air Quality – S240

G: Greenhouse i.e. Contribution to ozone depletion by adding to landfill

L: Land: (Possible contamination)

State Environmental Protection Policy – Contamination of Land – S95

Note:

SEPP’s (State Environmental Protection Policies) are now referenced in the new Environmental Protection Framework (2021-06)

2.4 Severity

Judgement of the overall level of environmental harm a hazard may cause:

CATASTROPHIC

Major emergency incident (e.g. toxic gas cloud) involving external

emergency services, major release of polluting substance(s), serious

breach of regulations which could lead to prosecution.

CRITICAL

Emergency involving high release of polluting substance(s) e.g. spill

of liquid from drums but not involving emergency services: major breach

of regulations leading to likely complaint by regulators and / or possible

prosecution.

MAJOR

Emergency involving significant release of polluting substance(s) e.g. spill

of liquid from drums but not involving emergency services: major breach

of regulations leading to likely complaint by regulators and / or possible

prosecution.

MINOR

Incident leading to moderate level of pollution (e.g. small quantity of toxic material discharged, or a larger quantity of less toxic material: breach of regulations which could lead to complaint by regulators if repeated).

NEGLIGIBLE

Incident involving infringement of regulations, but not significant

environmental effect (e.g. uncontrolled discharge of clean water to surface

water drains), complaint from regulators possible but unlikely.

2.5       Probability

Likelihood that the harm from a particular hazard and risk scenario may be

realized.

FREQUENT

Is expected to occur in most circumstances (daily)

REASONABLE / PROBABLE

Will probably occur in most circumstances (weekly exposure)

OCCASIONAL

Might occur at some time (weekly / monthly exposure)

REMOTE

Could occur at some time (monthly)

RARE

May occur in extraordinary circumstances

2.6	 Responsibilities

The Quality Manager is responsible for the development and upkeep of an Environmental Risk Assessment Program.

The Quality Manager along with the Operations Manager shall undertake Environmental Risk Assessments within Ultimate Laser.

Risk Assessments should be carried out at least for the following, as well as other facilities and hazards and a list maintained.

Risk of uncontrolled discharge to drains

Fire hazard, risk to air pollution

Risk of soil contamination

title: Incident / Accident Reporting Procedure
content:
INCIDENT / ACCIDENT REPORTING PROCEDURE

What to do when an accident / incident takes place:

Accidents on Site

Immediately seek medical attention for the injured person

Inform the Supervisor in charge of the work area as well as any Health and Safety Representatives and Ultimate Laser’s Operation Manager and or other Managers of the accident or injuries.

The Supervisor in charge of the work area shall where practicable take immediate action to isolate all accident media causing the accident (e.g. faulty slings or forklift etc.) from further use and investigate the cause of the fault.

Ultimate Lasers Register of Injuries Log

Injuries – First Aid

In the event that immediate attention is required, a qualified First Aid Officer is to be called. THE PATIENT MUST NOT BE LEFT UNATTENDED.

In the event of accidents, ambulance runs etc. the Supervisor in charge and others responsible must exert all possible effort to keep onlookers away from the scene. The only personnel required in such areas are those directly engaged in assisting in the emergency.

Employees must not attempt to remove foreign material from eyes. All eye injuries must be treated at a First Aid Centre or similar Medical Facility. In the case of chemical splash, it is vital, that the injured employee and others who are able to assist him/her, make sure that thorough and complete washing of the eye is accomplished.

If chemicals come into contact with the body, the affected parts must be washed with running water for at least fifteen minutes. To make sure that adequate washing is accomplished, shoes and clothing covering affected parts must be removed.

People who have not received the appropriate First Aid Training shall not treat or remove the injured. Where there is no trained First Aid person to assist, the medical service shall be contacted immediately and, in the meantime, the injured person shall be protected from further injury, influences of weather and loss of body temperature.

title: Emergency Response Procedure
content:
EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROCEDURE

EVACUATION STEPS

In the case of an emergency such as a Fire, Bomb Threat, Major Chemical Spill,

Gas Explosion or other emergency requiring the whole site to be evacuated, the following steps need to be followed by employees.

1) Warden contacted regarding emergency and with the Operation Manager’s decision made to evacuate the whole site.

2) Operation Manager contacts reception to request activation of alarms.

Types of Alarms:

Alert Signal – Single Horn

Evacuation Signal – Continuous Horn

3) Employees on hearing the Alert signal must:

Prepare to evacuate

Prepare to shut down services and machines

Remain at workplace

4) Employees on hearing the Evacuation signal must:

Shut down services and machines

All employees leave the building via the nearest exit and move to the nominated Evacuation Assembly Area and / or follow instructions from their Warden

Wardens do a “sweep” of the area to ensure all personnel have been evacuated from the area and close doors/windows where possible

5) At the Evacuation Assembly Area:

At the Evacuation Area, a nominated Warden will complete a check of employees as well as contractors and visitors who are on site at time of the evacuation (check visitors book i.e. visitors)

Wait in the safe Evacuation Assembly Area until the all clear is given by the Wardens to return to the building

Wardens will do a de-brief on the evacuation process and make recommendations to improve process if necessary.

NOMINATED WARDENS
